points: Under siege, Tzidkiyahu asks Yirmiyahu to daven. The people are relying on their alliance with Mitzrayim, and Yirmiyahu says it won't save them.
The lesson for today: we put too much trust in our allies. In the end everything comes from Hashem.
When the siege pauses, Yirmiyahu tries to leave for Binyamin. He's accused of defecting to Bavel, beaten and jailed.
Tzidkiyahu, a righteous king in a bad generation, moves him to a better jail and gives him a loaf of bread a day, even though Yirmiyahu still tells him he'll be handed to Bavel.

Why didn't Yirmiyahu leave earlier? Rashi: the city needed his tefillos. Like the Chofetz Chaim, who said don't move to America and then wrote a guide for those who did, a true leader stays with his people.
